answer: Go to sleep as soon as you feel drowsy, even if it is before noon; your body will repair lost sleep quickly. Avoid reading before bed because the light disrupts melatonin production, and instead watch TV or video games for a few hours to tire your eyes. Banish all blue light from your bedroom, even at night, because it tricks melatonin into stopping releas e. Sedatives are safe to use every night—they just help you fall asleep faster and are not addictive. Don’t bother with early-morning exercise; morning exercise speeds up sleep onset and improves quality.
